title: Classify Core and Backend Readiness Before Frontend Redesign
stopConditions: Project Control cannot identify the Work path, owner repository, Checklist target, or Evidence target before editing.
The matrix would claim production Backend readiness, broad Core readiness, broad Backend readiness, broad Editor readiness, or FlowDoc product readiness from bounded evidence.
An overloaded term such as node, document, record, draft, preview, ready, compatible, current, or live is used without the product terminology boundary.
The matrix would edit Core, Backend, or Editor product behavior instead of recording a Project Control readiness decision.
The next recommended lanes cannot be traced to an existing risk, blocker, or unknown in accepted evidence.
Project Control checks cannot validate the new document, records, generated index, or no-promotion boundary.
verificationTarget: Project Control records a bounded Core and Backend readiness matrix that supports frontend planning and next-lane selection while keeping FlowDoc planned and Core, Backend, and Editor unknown outside cited evidence.
summary: Done: Project Control now has a Core and Backend readiness matrix for pre-frontend planning, with explicit go/no-go decisions, risk and unknown classifications, and next owner-repository lanes.
